source.quote: To be specific, for every dollar Salesforce makes this year, the ecosystem will make $4.96. And that is expected to grow to $6.19 by 2026.

ecosystem.notes: The 10-K has no flow measure, so measure is null. Both studies are IDC white papers sponsored by Salesforce and are model-based forecasts, not measured flows. The December 2023 paper estimates new revenue generated for Salesforce customers from AI-powered Salesforce clouds (it also gives $312 billion for 2022, rising to a forecast $948 billion in 2028); the $2.02 trillion is cumulative over 2022–2028. The September 2021 paper is the one that sizes the partner ecosystem itself (add-on apps, IT services, consulting, hardware and more sold around Salesforce), as a ratio to Salesforce's own revenue ($4.96 per $1 in 2021); it has no single money value, so value is null. IDC notes "the ecosystem may include companies that are not formal business partners of Salesforce". Neither study covers FY2025 actuals.

footprint.notes: Salesforce publishes no state, country or regional breakdown of employees, offices, investment or taxes for FY2025. The 10-K (Item 2) gives about 0.9 million sq ft of leased and owned property in San Francisco used for its offices (plus about 2.1 million sq ft leased to others or available for lease), offices 'in various locations throughout the United States' and in Europe, North America, Asia, South America, Africa and Australia, and co-located data centers in the U.S., Europe and Asia, all without counts. The FY25 Stakeholder Impact Report gives 76,453 global employees with U.S.-only diversity data, and no geographic headcount. The IDC 'Salesforce Economy' white paper commissioned by Salesforce (Dec 2023) has no country table and only gives forecasts to 2028, so it was not used.
